proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemMechanics.composite
proposed_widenings.justification: The item has multiple independent mechanics families at once: passive held bonuses, charge-based spell activation, a triggered reaction, and a distinct destructive activation. The current magic-item record allows only one mechanics family.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "While you hold it, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls." / "While holding the staff, you can cast one of the spells..." / "you can take a Reaction when another creature casts a spell that targets only you." / "You can take a Magic action to break the staff..."

proposed_widenings.name: TriggeredReactionMechanics for magic items
proposed_widenings.justification: Spell Absorption is a genuine reaction-shaped item ability with a trigger and effect. Existing triggered-reaction support is spell-only, while activated magic items have no trigger grammar.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "you can take a Reaction when another creature casts a spell that targets only you"

proposed_widenings.name: charge_gain_from_absorbed_spell_level_with_overflow_branch
proposed_widenings.justification: The surface can spend charges and recharge at dawn, but it cannot gain charges from a reacted-to spell's level or branch on exceeding the pool cap into a second ability.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "the staff absorbs the magic of the spell, canceling its effect and gaining a number of charges equal to the absorbed spell's level. However, if doing so brings the staff's total number of charges above 50, the staff explodes as if you activated its Retributive Strike"

proposed_widenings.name: modify_damage_roll_numeric
proposed_widenings.justification: The passive quarterstaff rider grants a bonus to weapon damage rolls made with the item. Current atoms can modify AC, attack rolls, saves, and checks, but not damage rolls.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it"

notes: No content file was authored. The clean subsets already supported by the surface are outweighed by structural mismatch: one item contains passive, activation, triggered-reaction, and overflow-destruction mechanics. Retributive Strike also adds further pressure around area damage keyed to current charges and a random-plane avoidance branch.
